people.name: Tuan Nguyen
people.role: Principal Software Engineer; co-lead, Gemini app
people.status: Principal Software Engineer at Google DeepMind and co-lead of the Gemini app; announced computer use in the Gemini app for Mac on November 19, 2026.
people.short: Teaching Gemini to use a computer, from live phone demos to your Mac.
people.signal: Live phone demos (2024) → Galaxy S26 background control → Gemini app co-lead → computer use on Mac
people.why: **He connects UI grounding research with an assistant that quietly does the clicking for you.** His lessons for Gemini started with live phone demos in 2024, then moved to background computer control in a virtual app window on Samsung's Galaxy S26 and hands-free computer use from smart glasses. In 2026 he became a Principal Software Engineer at Google DeepMind and co-lead of the Gemini app, and after quarters of work on UI grounding and latency that pushed UI accuracy from 59.0% to 81.5%, the team shipped computer use in the Gemini app for Mac on November 19, 2026, running in its own background window so your cursor stays yours. Gemini's teacher, watching it graduate.

people.verifiedHow: Figma's October 15, 2026 Specs launch post is co-bylined by him as tech lead for Specs, and Figma's November 23, 2026 agent post names him the engineering lead on Specs.
people.short: Amazon's youngest engineer and Zeet founder, now tech lead for Figma Specs.
people.signal: Bebo → youngest engineer at Amazon (Twitch) → Zeet co-founder and CEO → Gather → Figma Specs
people.why: **He connects cloud plumbing with the plans that humans and agents now build from.** He became Amazon's youngest engineer after Twitch acquired Bebo, then co-founded Zeet, the Sequoia-backed deployment platform he ran as CEO. In early 2026 he joined Figma with the Gather team, and on October 15, 2026 Figma launched Specs, collaborative documents on the canvas that agents can read and build from, with him as tech lead. On November 23, 2026 Figma showed him using its agent to turn engineering crit feedback in FigJam into a draft spec. From deploys to decisions.

people.short: Building the harness that runs Claude agents, now on your own servers.
people.signal: Yammer → Lyft → Anthropic → Claude Managed Agents → self-hosted release
people.why: **She connects hard-won platform engineering with agents that can run wherever a company needs them.** After engineering roles at Yammer and Lyft, she joined Anthropic to build Claude Managed Agents, the hosted harness that keeps long-running Claude agents and their tools working at scale. In October 2026 she presented its architecture at the AI Engineer conference, and on November 12, 2026 her team shipped Self-Hosted Claude Managed Agents, putting the service inside a customer's own infrastructure. The harness, now portable.

He then founded Hercules, which Codeship Labs reports is a seven-person company doing tens of millions in revenue by letting non-coders build their business software, and on November 19, 2026 he launched Hercules Agents, which learn from their own run history. From the terminal to the front office.
